findings.title: [P1] Execute the branch through an argv array, not a shell string
findings.body: `src/git.ts:7-8` interpolates `branch` into `git show ${branch}` and passes it to `execAsync` (promisified `exec`, which runs the string through `/bin/sh -c`). Any caller-supplied value containing shell metacharacters executes as shell syntax: `showBranch("HEAD; id")` runs `id`, and `$(...)`/backticks allow arbitrary command execution with the process's credentials. These are valid Git ref names (`;`, `$`, backticks are not prohibited by `check-ref-format`), so even well-formed branch data can trigger this, and untrusted input (e.g. remote ref names or PR-derived strings) makes it exploitable. The previous `execFileAsync("git", ["show", branch])` was immune because the value crossed no shell boundary. Restore the argv-array call.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve single-argument semantics for empty and metacharacter inputs
findings.body: Removing the argv boundary changes results for edge inputs. With `branch === ""`, the old call passed an empty revision argument and rejected; the new command becomes bare `git show`, which succeeds and shows `HEAD`. A value like `"HEAD --stat"` previously failed as one invalid revision and now expands into multiple valid arguments. Refs containing spaces, `$`, or quotes are also silently mangled by shell parsing. This contradicts the PR's stated goal of preserving existing contracts.

findings.title: [P3] Dead code: `execFileAsync` wrapper and `execFile` import are now unused
findings.body: After this PR, `execFileAsync` (line 4) has no remaining usage anywhere in the repository — `showBranch` was its only consumer — so the wrapper and the `execFile` import on line 1 are dead code. This trips `noUnusedLocals`/unused-import lint checks in consuming projects. Remove them or (preferably, per the P1 finding) revert `showBranch` to use `execFileAsync`.

findings.title: [P3] Missing-git error contract changed from ENOENT to shell exit 127
findings.body: When `git` is absent from `PATH`, `execFileAsync` rejected with a spawn error (`code: "ENOENT"`); `execAsync` successfully spawns the shell and instead rejects with the shell's command-not-found exit status (typically 127) and shell-generated stderr. Callers that detect a missing Git installation via `ENOENT` no longer work. Worth documenting or fixing by keeping the direct spawn.

findings.title: [P3] maxBuffer overflow now kills the shell, not Git, on non-execing shells
findings.body: When output exceeds `exec`'s default 1 MiB `maxBuffer`, Node kills the spawned shell process rather than Git itself. On POSIX `/bin/sh` typically execs a single simple command in place (same PID), so behavior is unchanged there, but on Windows (`cmd /d /s /c`) and other shells that retain a wrapper process, Git can outlive the promise rejection and keep running/writing after callers believe the operation ended. `git show` output can easily exceed 1 MiB, making this reachable.

findings.title: [P3] Avoid launching a shell for every Git invocation
findings.body: Each `showBranch` call now spawns and parses an extra shell process before Git runs — work `execFile` avoided. For a per-call subprocess helper this adds avoidable startup latency and CPU pressure in high-frequency or concurrent callers.
